environment: Jeeves runtime with real model and offline fixture search/fetch. One sample per arm, not live-web or autonomous discovery evidence.
observations: Traffic-first and TEU-first both performed two searches that returned the same candidate set, then fetched access and TEU. The vessel record was visible but not read within the cap. Both marked it unresolved instead of claiming full recovery.

The withheld-TEU arm did not confirm throughput. It read access and vessel evidence but discounted both abbreviated fixture pages as placeholders; it also introduced unverified background from memory. That arm does not pass the partial-answer rubric, and the fixture realism limits interpretation.

The real model resumed after a scripted checkpoint and fetched the missing throughput and access. It also read a mirror of the already opened traffic source. The resulting report distinguishes all three measures and recognizes the mirror relationship, but its wording overstates some evidence and its task ended Failed. The exact final acceptance checks were not captured in this first run; successful artifact writing is not task acceptance.

The experiment shows a practical need to count genuinely new candidates and track per-question evidence, not just raise a call limit. It does not isolate natural search recall or establish a general ranking effect.
